questions.question: According to the article, what was the approximate timing of the formation of the Panamanian land bridge that connected South America to North America?
options: Approximately 3 million years ago
Approximately 35 million years ago
Approximately 110 million years ago
Approximately 66 million years ago
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'approximately 3 million years ago, South America became connected to North America when the Bolivar Trough marine barrier disappeared and the Panamanian land bridge formed.'
Incorrect. The article places the separation of Antarctica and South America around 35 mya, not the formation of the Panamanian land bridge.
Incorrect. The article dates the divergence of South America and Africa along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge to around 110 mya, which is unrelated to the Panamanian land bridge.
Incorrect. The article associates 66 mya with the mass-extinction of dinosaurs and the rise of neotropical rainforest biomes, not with the formation of the Panamanian land bridge.

questions.question: Based on the article, what was the first species known to have migrated northward from South America to North America during the Great American Interchange?
options: Pliometanastes, a fossil ground sloth roughly the size of a modern black bear
Megatherium, a ground sloth
Titanis, a terror bird
Pampatherium, a giant armadillo
answer_explanations: Correct. The article explicitly states: 'The first species known to have made the northward migration was Pliometanastes, a fossil ground sloth roughly the size of a modern black bear.'
Incorrect. Megatherium is listed among species that followed the route north during the Irvingtonian stage around 1.9 mya, not as the first northward migrant.
Incorrect. Titanis is described as having dispersed into North America, but the article does not identify it as the first species to migrate northward.
Incorrect. Pampatherium is mentioned as one of the species that migrated north during the Irvingtonian stage around 1.9 mya, not as the first northward migrant.

questions.question: Based on the article, what does genomic research indicate about the initial peopling of South America?
options: It involved at least three major population dispersals rather than a single continuous migration
It involved a single continuous migration from North America
It involved exactly two major population dispersals
It involved only one major population dispersal
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'Genomic research indicates that the initial peopling of South America involved at least three major population dispersals rather than a single continuous migration.'
Incorrect. The article explicitly rejects the idea of a single continuous migration, stating instead that there were at least three major population dispersals.
Incorrect. The article states 'at least three major population dispersals,' not exactly two.
Incorrect. The article states 'at least three major population dispersals,' not only one.

questions.question: According to the article, what happened to the biodiversity of South America during the approximately 30 million years when it was an isolated island-continent?
options: Species evolved within the continent in isolation from the rest of the world
Species from North America migrated south and replaced native species
Biodiversity remained unchanged from the rest of the world
Marine species dominated the continent's ecosystems
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'During approximately 30 million years, the biodiversity of South America was isolated from the rest of the world, leading to the evolution of species within the continent.'
Incorrect. The article describes South America as isolated during this period; North American species arrived later after the Panamanian land bridge formed.
Incorrect. The article states that isolation led to the evolution of species within the continent, not that biodiversity remained unchanged from the rest of the world.
Incorrect. The article does not state that marine species dominated the continent's ecosystems during this period.

questions.question: Based on the article, what was the result of the Great American Interchange in terms of species extinction?
options: The expansion of North American fauna caused a mass extinction in which hundreds of South American species disappeared in a relatively short time
South American species caused a mass extinction of North American species
No extinctions occurred; all species coexisted successfully
Only plant species went extinct, while animal species were unaffected
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'The result of the expansion of a North American fauna was a mass extinction in which hundreds of species disappeared in a relatively short time.'
Incorrect. The article states that North American fauna expanded and caused the extinction, not that South American species caused extinctions in North America.
Incorrect. The article explicitly states that a mass extinction occurred in which hundreds of species disappeared.
Incorrect. The article does not state that only plant species went extinct; it refers broadly to hundreds of species disappearing.
